_about: Harbor Now daily publisher settings (scripts/harbor-daily.mjs). Owner decision 2026-11-25: Harbor Now covers only the symbols on Rosie's own watchlists, no outside news. The four index funds are context only.
_data_level: "words" (default): no market numbers on the page, only words (rose, slipped, most, a few). "pct": adds rounded percent changes (about 0.5%). Switch to "pct" only after the lawyer clears it. Prices are never published in either mode.
_provider: "auto": Tiingo end-of-day prices when the TIINGO_API_TOKEN secret is set, otherwise Yahoo Finance's public chart endpoint. VIX always comes from Yahoo (^VIX). Neither source licenses public display of raw prices, which is why the page shows words (or rounded % in pct mode) and never prices.

watchlist_i._source: Rosie's Watchlist I panel: SEED_ORDER in nrini49/schwab trade_universe.py = PERMITTED_ORDER in nrini49/interactive (main, read 2026-11-25). Index funds are left out here (context only), and so are crypto (BTC, ETH, XRP: 24-hour markets with no NYSE close; XRP stays off everything public) and SQQQ (tradable, never on the panel). Re-sync when Rosie's list changes.

watchlist_ii._source: Rosie's Watchlist II seed: candidates.json in nrini49/interactive and nrini49/schwab (main, read 2026-11-25), minus the index funds. Watchlist II is seeded partly from outside mentions, so it is described as a group only (name_symbols false): Harbor Now never re-posts anyone's picks. Re-sync when candidates.json changes.

_min_coverage: The run fails (and GitHub emails the owner) if fewer than this share of a list's symbols have both closes, or if any index fund or VIX is missing.
_sector_funds: The eleven SPDR sector ETFs (Rosie's Lime Sniper SECTOR_ETFS) plus SMH for semiconductors. The hot sector is ranked the way Rosie's sector funnel ranks it: strength against SPY over recent sessions plus today's. Member lists: data/sector-members.json.
_convergence: Three legs, from Rosie's own rules on daily closes: (1) the four index funds rising, (2) the hot sector rising with them, (3) the strongest rising names inside the hot sector, Watchlist I names first, then Rosie's sector member list. 'Rising' is the daily form of Lime Sniper's all-three-rising filter: close above its trend average and that average pointing up. Trend colours use Rosie's regime averages. The page describes these in plain words and never prints the periods or weights.
